question: The division of subjects between the Union and the States is laid out in which Schedule of the Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Schedule IX
Schedule V
Schedule X
Schedule VII
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Schedule VII

Explanation:
The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution divides legislative powers between the Union and the States. It contains three lists: the Union List (100 subjects of national importance, e.g., defense, foreign affairs), the State List (61 subjects of regional significance, e.g., police, agriculture), and the Concurrent List (52 subjects where both can legislate, e.g., education, forests). This division establishes a federal structure, ensuring a clear demarcation of powers. The Union List takes precedence in case of conflict with the State List, while the Concurrent List allows cooperative legislation. The Seventh Schedule is crucial for understanding India's federal system and the distribution of authority between the central and state governments.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Seventh Schedule → Divides subjects into Union, State, and Concurrent Lists
☛ Total subjects in Union List → 100 (originally 97, amended)
☛ Total subjects in State List → 61 (originally 66)
☛ Total subjects in Concurrent List → 52 (originally 47)
☛ Latest addition to Concurrent List → Goods and Services Tax (GST) via 101st Amendment (2016)
question_hi: संघ और राज्यों के बीच विषयों का विभाजन संविधान की किस अनुसूची में निर्धारित है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)

अनुसूची V
अनुसूची X
अनुसूची VII
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुसूची VII

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की सातवीं अनुसूची (Schedule VII) में संघ और राज्यों के बीच विधायी शक्तियों का विभाजन किया गया है। इसमें तीन सूचियाँ हैं: संघ सूची (केंद्र सरकार के अधिकार क्षेत्र के 100 विषय), राज्य सूची (राज्य सरकारों के 61 विषय), और समवर्ती सूची (दोनों के 52 विषय)। संघ सूची में रक्षा, विदेश मामले, परमाणु ऊर्जा जैसे राष्ट्रीय महत्व के विषय शामिल हैं। राज्य सूची में कृषि, पुलिस, स्थानीय सरकार जैसे क्षेत्रीय विषय हैं। समवर्ती सूची में शिक्षा, वन, वन्यजीव संरक्षण जैसे विषय आते हैं, जिन पर दोनों स्तरों की सरकारें कानून बना सकती हैं। यह विभाजन संघीय ढांचे को मजबूती प्रदान करता है और शक्तियों का संतुलन सुनिश्चित करता है।

question: Which amendment granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Seventy-fourth Amendment Act, 1992
Eighty-sixth Amendment Act, 2002
Seventy-third Amendment Act, 1992
Seventy-second Amendment Act, 1992
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Seventy-third Amendment Act, 1992

Explanation:
The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions in India. It added Part IX and Articles 243 to 243-O to the Constitution, relating to Panchayats. The amendment came into force on 24 April 1993. It ensured the formation, functions, powers, and financial authority of Panchayats. The Gram Sabha was given constitutional recognition, and provisions were made for reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women. The 74th Amendment deals with urban local bodies, while the 86th Amendment relates to the Right to Education.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Amendment that gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj → 73rd Amendment Act, 1992
☛ Part added by the 73rd Amendment → Part IX
☛ Date of enforcement of the 73rd Amendment → 24 April 1993
☛ Amendment that provided for Gram Sabha in Panchayati Raj → 73rd Amendment
☛ Amendment giving constitutional status to urban local bodies → 74th Amendment Act, 1992

question: Which of the following commissions was appointed to look into the question of states based on language? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Gadgil Commission
Sarkaria Commission
Swaran Singh Committee
Dhar Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dhar Commission

Explanation:
The question of reorganisation of states on linguistic basis was first referred to the Dhar Commission (Linguistic Provinces Commission) in 1948. This commission was appointed by the Government of India under the chairmanship of Justice S. K. Dhar. The commission rejected the idea of language as the sole basis for state reorganisation. Subsequently, the Fazal Ali Commission was formed in 1953, leading to the States Reorganisation Act of 1956. Gadgil Commission is related to river water disputes, Sarkaria Commission to centre-state relations, and Swaran Singh Committee to fundamental duties.

☛ Gadgil Commission is related to? → River water disputes
☛ Sarkaria Commission is related to? → Centre-state relations
question_hi: भाषा के आधार पर राज्यों के प्रश्न पर विचार करने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा आयोग नियुक्त किया गया था? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)

Explanation:

question: What was the main objective of the Pitt’s India Act of 1784, passed by the British Parliament? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Empower provincial councils
Trade monopoly
Abolish company rule
Establish dual government
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Establish dual government

Explanation:
The Pitt's India Act of 1784, passed by the British Parliament, aimed to address the maladministration of the East India Company. Its main objective was to establish a dual system of government in India by creating a Board of Control in Britain to oversee political and military affairs, while the Company's Court of Directors retained commercial functions. This act amended the Regulating Act of 1773 and increased British government control over Indian affairs. By separating commercial and political powers, it sought to curb the company's mismanagement and introduce greater parliamentary supervision. Thus, establishing a dual government was the core purpose of the Pitt's India Act, making 'establish dual government' the correct answer.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Who headed the Board of Control? → British Chancellor of the Exchequer
☛ What system did Pitt's India Act introduce? → Dual government
☛ Which act did Pitt's India Act amend? → Regulating Act of 1773
☛ Which two bodies comprised the dual government? → Court of Directors and Board of Control

question: How did Public Interest Litigation (PIL) emerge in India as a tool of judicial activism? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: It originated under the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976).
It was introduced by the Lok Adalat system in 2005.
It began in 1979 when the Supreme Court allowed individuals to file cases for public interest.
It was first used during the Emergency (1975-77).
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It began in 1979 when the Supreme Court allowed individuals to file cases for public interest.

Explanation:
Public Interest Litigation (PIL) emerged in India in 1979 as a tool of judicial activism, when the Supreme Court allowed individuals and groups to file cases in public interest. It evolved after the Emergency (1975-77) to protect the fundamental rights of citizens. Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer pioneered this concept. The first major PIL case was Sunil Batra v. Delhi Administration (1980), addressing the plight of prisoners. PIL simplified access to justice for the poor and marginalized, even accepting epistolary jurisdiction (letters as petitions).

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Year PIL started in India? → 1979
☛ Father of PIL in India? → Justice P.N. Bhagwati
☛ First PIL case? → Sunil Batra v. Delhi Administration (1980)
☛ What type of petition is accepted in PIL? → Letter petition (Epistolary jurisdiction)
☛ PIL is based on which principle? → Judicial activism
question_hi: भारत में पब्लिक इंटरेस्ट लिटिगेशन ( PIL ) न्यायिक सक्रियता के एक उपकरण के रूप में कैसे उभरी? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: यह 42वें संवैधानिक संशोधन (1976) के तहत उत्पन्न हुई।

इसका पहली बार उपयोग आपातकाल (1975-77) के दौरान किया गया था।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है यह 1979 में शुरू हुआ जब सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने व्यक्तियों को जनहित के लिए मामले दर्ज करने की अनुमति दी।

Explanation:
भारत में पब्लिक इंटरेस्ट लिटिगेशन (PIL) का उद्भव 1979 में हुआ, जब सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने न्यायिक सक्रियता के तहत व्यक्तियों और समूहों को जनहित के मामले दर्ज करने की अनुमति दी। यह आपातकाल (1975-77) के बाद नागरिकों के मौलिक अधिकारों की रक्षा के लिए शुरू हुआ। जस्टिस पी.एन. भगवती और जस्टिस वी.आर. कृष्णा अय्यर ने इस अवधारणा को विकसित किया। पहला महत्वपूर्ण PIL मामला सुनील बत्रा बनाम दिल्ली प्रशासन (1980) था, जिसमें कैदियों की दुर्दशा पर ध्यान दिया गया। PIL ने गरीबों और वंचितों तक न्याय की पहुंच को सरल बनाया, क्योंकि इसमें पत्र याचिका को भी स्वीकार किया गया।

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution specifically deal with the establishment of Tribunals for administrative and other matters?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Articles 323A and 323B
Articles 32 and 226
Articles 356C and 360D
Articles 14 and 15
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Articles 323A and 323B

Explanation:
Part XIV-A of the Indian Constitution, comprising Articles 323A and 323B, specifically deals with the establishment of Tribunals. Article 323A empowers Parliament to establish Administrative Tribunals for adjudicating disputes related to public services. Article 323B allows state governments to establish tribunals for other matters such as taxation, land reforms, elections, etc. These articles were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). Articles 32 and 226 empower the Supreme Court and High Courts respectively to issue writs for enforcement of fundamental rights, while Articles 14 and 15 relate to the right to equality.

question: The __________ of the Indian Constitution protects laws from being challenged in courts under judicial review. (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Eleventh Schedule
Ninth Schedule
Fifth Schedule
Third Schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ninth Schedule

Explanation:
The Ninth Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides protection to laws from being challenged in courts under judicial review. It was added by the First Amendment in 1951 to shield land reform laws from litigation. Under Article 31B, laws placed in this Schedule cannot be declared invalid even if they violate fundamental rights. However, in the landmark case of I.R. Coelho vs State of Tamil Nadu (2007), the Supreme Court ruled that laws in the Ninth Schedule are still subject to judicial review if they violate the basic structure of the Constitution. Initially containing 13 laws, the Ninth Schedule now includes over 284 laws, covering various socio-economic reforms. This Schedule acts as a protective umbrella but with limitations regarding constitutional basic structure.

☛ Which Article is related to the Ninth Schedule? → Article 31B
☛ From which protection do Ninth Schedule laws benefit? → Judicial review

☛ How many laws are currently in the Ninth Schedule? → Over 284

question: Providing immediate assistance during a disaster is classified under which stage of disaster management? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Relief response
Prevention
Reconstruction
Preparation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Relief response

Explanation:
Disaster management consists of four main phases: Prevention, Preparedness, Response, and Recovery/Reconstruction. Providing immediate assistance during a disaster falls under the Response phase. This phase includes rescue operations, medical aid, distribution of food and water, shelter provision, and immediate relief to affected people. The Prevention phase occurs before a disaster, Preparedness involves pre-disaster planning, and Reconstruction is post-relief work. Therefore, immediate assistance is part of Relief response.

question: Which legal authority gives statutory status to Lok Adalats in India?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act
The Civil Procedure Code
The Indian Penal Code
The Legal Services Authorities Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Legal Services Authorities Act

Explanation:
In India, Lok Adalats derive their statutory status from the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. This Act provides for the constitution of legal services authorities at the national, state, district, and taluka levels. Lok Adalats serve as a platform for the amicable settlement of disputes, and their awards are considered equivalent to a decree of a Civil Court, which are final and binding on all parties. The Act also emphasizes the provision of free legal aid to weaker sections of society, ensuring access to justice for all.

question: Which Amendment is considered a near rewrite of the Constitution and made changes to the Preamble, Schedule VII and 53 Articles? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: 42nd Amendment
38th Amendment
44th Amendment
86th Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd Amendment

Explanation:
The 42nd Amendment (1976) is the most comprehensive amendment to the Indian Constitution, often called the 'Mini-Constitution'. It added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble. It made changes to Schedule VII (Union, State, and Concurrent Lists). A total of 53 Articles were amended, including the addition of Fundamental Duties (Article 51A), extension of President's rule duration, and curtailment of judicial review. This amendment gave the executive greater control over the judiciary. Later, the 44th Amendment (1978) reversed many of its provisions.

☛ Which three words were added to the Preamble? → Socialist, Secular, Integrity

☛ What is the 42nd Amendment also known as? → Mini-Constitution

question: Which of the following major events followed the death of Potti Sreeramulu?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Creation of linguistic minorities commission
Appointment of the States Reorganisation Commission
Formation of the Planning Commission
Formation of the Election Commission

Explanation:
Potti Sreeramulu died in 1952 after a 58-day hunger strike demanding the formation of Andhra state. His death triggered widespread protests across the country. In response, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru appointed the States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) in 1953, headed by Fazal Ali. The SRC submitted its report in 1955, leading to the States Reorganisation Act of 1956, which reorganised states on linguistic lines. Sreeramulu's death was a turning point in the linguistic states movement in India.

question: What is the nature of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 3)

Both the Centre and the States can legislate
Only during emergencies

Explanation:
The Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution contains 52 subjects on which both the Centre and the States can legislate. It is part of the division of powers between the Union and the States. This ensures national uniformity while allowing state flexibility. Key subjects include education, forests, and labor welfare. The list promotes cooperative federalism.

question: Which type of Municipality is formed for a transitional area under Article 243Q of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Nagar Panchayat
Town Panchayat
Municipal Council
Municipal Corporation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nagar Panchayat

Explanation:
Under Article 243Q of the Indian Constitution, a Nagar Panchayat is constituted for a transitional area (an area in transition from rural to urban). This provision was added through the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992. A Nagar Panchayat is an urban local body that exists in the transition phase between rural and urban areas. The Constitution specifies three types of municipalities: Nagar Panchayat (for transitional area), Municipal Council (for smaller urban area), and Municipal Corporation (for larger urban area). Members of a Nagar Panchayat are directly elected by the people, and it has a chairperson. The exact classification of a transitional area is determined by the state government based on factors like population and density.

question: Which Article gives the President of India the power to grant pardons and reprieves?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 72
Article 76
Article 74
Article 75
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 72

Explanation:
Article 72 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment. This power applies to persons convicted under union laws or sentences by court-martial. For state offenses, the Governor has similar power under Article 161. The President's clemency power is subject to judicial review, as established in the Maru Ram vs. Union of India case. It is an executive power exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers. The scope includes pardon (complete remission), reprieve (temporary stay), respite (less severe substitute), remission (reduction), and commutation (change to lighter punishment).

संविधान (छियासीवां संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2002 ने मौलिक कर्तव्यों में एक नया कर्तव्य जोड़ा। अनुच्छेद 51A में खंड (k) जोड़ा गया, जिसके अनुसार माता-पिता या संरक्षक का कर्तव्य है कि वे अपने 6 से 14 वर्ष की आयु के बच्चों को शिक्षा के अवसर प्रदान करें। यह संशोधन शिक्षा के अधिकार को मौलिक अधिकार बनाने की दिशा में एक कदम था, जिसे बाद में 2009 में शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम (RTE) के रूप में लागू किया गया। अन्य विकल्प जैसे वैज्ञानिक दृष्टिकोण (खंड h), राष्ट्रीय एकता (खंड c), और पर्यावरण संरक्षण (खंड g) पहले से मौजूद कर्तव्य हैं।

question: The maximum interval between two sessions of state assembly can be ____. (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: 3 months
6 months
9 months
12 months
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 6 months

Explanation:
According to Article 174 of the Indian Constitution, the maximum interval between two sessions of a state legislative assembly cannot exceed 6 months. This provision is similar to Article 85 for the Parliament. The Governor summons and prorogues the sessions of the state assembly from time to time. This ensures that the assembly meets at least twice a year, maintaining democratic accountability. If the gap between two sessions exceeds 6 months, it would be considered a constitutional violation. The provision aims to ensure continuous legislative oversight and prevent executive overreach.
